changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8318-jsdoc-default-tag-corrections.md`

- names `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > - `CRUDDialogSchema.size` / `.closeOnOutsideClick` / `.closeOnEscape` / `.showClose` — there is no `register('crud-dialog'` anywhere, so no node of that type ever reaches a renderer. Recorded once on the interface. Per key, the name census differs: two spellings occur nowhere outside the declaration and its zod twin, and `showClose`'s one other occurrence (`renderers/overlay/drawer.tsx:38`) belongs to `DrawerSchema`. - `ActionSchema.level` — `type: 'action'` is not a rendered node type, and `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, which is what makes `method` / `chainMode` / `reload` / `close` live, does not read `level`. - `CardSchema.variant` — `card` IS registered, twice, and neither registration reads it: the `ui` route forwards the key to `ui/card.tsx`, which spreads onto a `div` and mentions `variant` nowhere, and the `page` route forwards only its designer props. - `PageNodeSchema.isDefault` — `page` IS registered, and `PageRenderer` neither reads the key nor forwards it: the wrapper element gets `toDomProps(props)`, an allow-list that does not carry it.

### `.changeset/action-keys-warning-text-5642.md`

- names `ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > Both halves of the message's tail had outlived the change they described. It told the author the key was warned about rather than rejected because `ActionDef` "still carries `[key: string]: any`" — objectstack#4075 step 3 deleted that index signature, and `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` pins the deletion in the opposite direction (`{ ActionDef: false, ActionContext: true }`), while `actionDef-closed-surface.test.ts` pins that `tsc` now rejects exactly such a key at the construction site. And it prescribed promoting the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` "(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts)" — that file holds the INVENTORY (`ACTION_DEF_KEYS`); the interface is in `ActionRunner.ts`. The wrong pointer had teeth: an author who followed it edited the inventory alone, which is precisely the half-change the pin test reddens on, since it re-derives the inventory from the interface's AST.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `d1e683fa1` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1755 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2361 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36594426592)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `251bd2a053f15d7fc3a84b43977026645c36d36b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11082 (body; triage `5888840929`; claim `5892961994`; os-dev-report `5893910327`), PR #11121 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), and the head's check-runs with `filter=latest`. Context reads were `contents/PATH?ref=HEAD` only.

Gate verdicts (the head's check-runs, `filter=latest`, read again after the last run had completed): 43 runs, 40 success, 3 skipped (`dependabot` and the two coverage matrix jobs the workflow skips on a PR), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Success includes Test (shard 1/8 through 8/8), Test (dist pins), Type Check, Lint, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Doc Snippet Type Check, README Export Check, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Overwrite Report, Line Citation Gate, Inert vi.mock Specifier Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec Main Shape Gate, Skill Example Check and Bundle Analysis.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`captureUpdateUndoData` becomes a named export of `@object-ui/core` — right.** Signature unchanged: `captureUpdateUndoData(writtenFields: readonly string[], rowRecord)` on a string-keyed record, answering the string-keyed snapshot or `undefined`. The body is byte-identical (`every(rowCarries)`, then `Object.fromEntries`). It reaches the package entry through the existing `export * from './ActionRunner.js'` in `actions/index.ts` and `export * from './actions/index.js'` in `src/index.ts`, so no barrel line changed. `rowCarries` remains a module-private function: declared without `export`, re-exported nowhere. The docblock's added paragraph names the two external callers and the per-field idiom `captureUpdateUndoData([field], rowRecord) === undefined`; both statements are true on the head. Pinned through the package entry by `captureUpdateUndoData.export-11082.test.ts` (identity with the runner module's own function; carried values; carried `null`; absent field; partial set; own key holding `undefined`; inherited key).

2. **`RecordDetailView`'s `api` handler (generic `default` branch) — right, and it matches the two siblings limb by limb.**
   - Written set: `Object.keys(params)`, where `params` is `action.params` with `_rowRecord` deleted and `bodyExtra` merged last — exactly the payload the write then sends (`dataSource.update(targetObject, String(targetId), params)`). The runner's `writtenFields` (keys of `patch` under `collected`, minus `_rowRecord` and `recordId`) and the console runtime's `fields` (params minus `_rowRecord` and `recordId`, plus `bodyExtra`) are each that surface's own payload in the same way.
   - Uncarried: `undoData` is `undefined`, no `undo` is put on the result, `ActionRunner.handlePostExecution` pushes nothing to `globalUndoManager` and calls the toast handler with `undo: undefined`, and the view's `toastHandler` then renders `toast.success` with no `action` — no Undo button. Same outcome as the runner and the console runtime.
   - The `console.warn` fires only after `await dataSource.update` resolves, which is both siblings' "succeeded but offers no Undo" timing, with the same `{ action: action.name, missing }` payload; the message differs only in its last sentence, which names this surface's carry rule (the reader's field-level read) instead of the list row's (`$select` plus FLS) — the true statement here. `missing` is derived per field through the helper, not through a second predicate.
   - Carried `null` is captured as `null`; a carried value as itself. `redoData: { ...params }` is unchanged. The `description` fallback that objectui#11080 owns (`action.label`, else the literal `Undo` followed by the target object's name) is byte-identical, moved two columns right.
   - The capture is computed before the write, as it was before this PR; `pageRecord` is React state the write does not mutate, so the order is immaterial. The `notifyRecordChanged()`-when-`undo` tail is unchanged. The diff removes one `as any` (on `pageRecord`) and adds none; `undo` stays `any` as before.

3. **`useConsoleActionRuntime` moved onto the helper — right, behaviour unchanged.** Old limbs: `missing = written.filter(k: not hasOwnProperty(rowRecord, k) or rowRecord[k] === undefined)`; `missing.length === 0` gates; `undoData = Object.fromEntries(written.map(k: [k, rowRecord[k]]))`; else the warn with `missing`. New: `undoData = captureUpdateUndoData(written, rowRecord)`, whose `rowCarries` is that same `hasOwnProperty and not undefined` predicate and whose success answer is that same `Object.fromEntries` map — so `undoData` is defined exactly when `missing` was empty and holds the same entries. `if (undoData)` is a safe gate: a defined answer is always an object, and `written` is non-empty by the enclosing guard that requires at least one key in `fields`. The else limb's `missing = written.filter(k: captureUpdateUndoData([k], rowRecord) === undefined)` equals the old filter field by field. Warn text and payload, the write-before-capture order, the `undo` id/description/`redoData: { ...fields }` are all untouched. The objectui#10404 pin `useConsoleActionRuntime.undoAbsentField-10404.test.tsx` is unchanged and still in the tree.

4. **`packages/core/README.md` section — right.** A `###` section beside the existing per-helper sections; its three example answers (`{ status: 'open' }`, `{ status: null }`, `undefined`) match the helper, and its carry definition and no-partial rule restate the docblock. README Export Check on the head: success.

5. **Pins in objectui#10404's shape — right.** `RecordDetailView.undoCapture-11082.test.tsx` runs the real view, the real runner, the view's own handlers and the real `useGlobalUndo`: an uncarried written field gives no Undo button, nothing on the undo stack, the write still happens, and the warn carries `missing: ['status']`; a carried field beside an uncarried one gives no Undo at all; a carried `null` is restored by an Undo write of `{ status: null }`; a carried value by `{ status: 'open' }`. The ablation the PR body reports (the pre-fix loop turns the uncarried and partial cases red and leaves the two `?? null`-correct cases green) is the pattern the rule predicts.

6. **Nothing else on the public surface moved.** The `ActionRunner.ts` hunk is the `export` keyword and docblock lines only; no type, key, accepted value or other symbol changes. `@object-ui/react` (`useGlobalUndo`, `UndoManager`) is untouched; `@object-ui/app-shell` exports nothing new.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes` — confirmed; the PR body's line and the changeset's line both say so, with the reason. `'@object-ui/core': minor` is right for a new published symbol whose answers do not change; `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` is right for a behaviour fix with no surface change; `@object-ui/react` correctly takes no bump (no file of it changed). No other export or type moved (① item 6). Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read and Changeset Overwrite Report: all success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report `5893910327`), each answered:
1. README section added — accepted. The README documents exported helpers section by section, AGENTS.md #2 asks for docs with a feature, and `check:readme-exports` now judges this import (green on the head).
2. `console.warn` in `RecordDetailView` — accepted. Zone 2 item 4 asks for parity with the console runtime; the runner and the runtime both give this diagnostic, in this shape, at this point (after the successful write). Not a surface change.
3. The PR body's `#2` autolink to objectui#2 — cosmetic. It is not a closing keyword (`Fixes #11082` is the only one), so it changes nothing about what merges; the seat may reword it when the draft is lifted. Not a contract matter.
4. One lock hold for the type-checks and the docs-scope build, reporting batch-last-exit — process note; each part's own exit code was recorded. No contract effect.
5. objectui#11080's fallback line re-indented — confirmed byte-identical in the diff; the serial constraint on #11080 was already declared in the claim. No contract effect.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Out-of-scope inference (carrier none; judged here, not widened into this PR):
- **Read on the head, the inference holds.** `RecordDetailView` reads the page record with `$expand` on every reference-bearing field the principal may read (`buildExpandFields(objectDef.fields)` filtered by `perms.checkField`, `:560`–`:564`). objectql's `expandRelatedRecords` replaces the id in place under the SAME key (`record[fieldName] = recordMap.get(String(val)) ?? val`), and the view's own comment at `:1373` already says `$expand` "substituted" the stored foreign key on this surface. `captureUpdateUndoData` answers `rowRecord[field]` verbatim, and `useGlobalUndo.executeOp` hands `op.undoData` to `dataSource.update` unchanged. So an undoable record-page action that writes a `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` / `tree` field captures the expanded object as the prior value, and pressing Undo sends that object back as the field's new value.
- **Whether the route accepts it** (objectstack `record-validator`): a reference slot is judged by `ReferenceIdValueSchema` — an id string, never an embedded record. Under the ADR-0104 strict posture (`OS_DATA_VALUE_SHAPE_STRICT_ENABLED`, or a deployment whose `adr-0104-value-shapes` gate is closed) the write is refused with `invalid_value_shape`: Undo fails and the user sees the error toast. Under the default lenient posture the write is admitted, tallied and logged, so the lookup slot then STORES the expanded object — the corruption `os migrate value-shapes` exists to find. Either way it is a real defect at a public door: any `undoable` `type: 'api'` action on the record page whose params or `bodyExtra` write a reference field. The list surfaces share it wherever the grid `$expand`s the written column, since the runner and the console runtime hand their row through the same helper.
- **Pre-existing, not introduced here.** The pre-fix `pageRecord[k] ?? null` captured the same expanded object; this PR neither adds nor removes the exposure. The seat files it.
